mainTopic: A קטן's action and intention, intent in שחיטת קדשים, and slaughter by a נכרי or a מין
overview: This עמוד opens in the middle of a question רבי יוחנן raised about a קטן. A משנה says a קטן has 'action' but no 'thought,' so why ask? רבי חייא בר אבא explains that the question is about thought that shows in a child's actions, like walking a עולה to the north and slaughtering it there. רבי אמי objects that רבי יוחנן already ruled that a child who turns his produce over in the dew does count. The answer is that the question was whether this counts מדאורייתא or only מדרבנן. In a second version, רבי יוחנן asks whether a קטן even has legal action. That version ends with a clear ruling: action counts by Torah law, plain thought never counts, and thought shown in action counts only מדרבנן. Next, שמואל and רב הונא find the פסוק showing that a מתעסק disqualifies קדשים even after the fact. Then a new משנה teaches that a נכרי's slaughter makes a נבלה. רבי יוחנן says this does not follow רבי אליעזר. רבי אמי reads it as a contrast with a מין, whose slaughter counts as עבודה זרה, and a ברייתא listing a מין's items continues onto the next עמוד.

steps.title: The משנה says a minor has no legal thought
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of a משנה brought against רבי יוחנן's question: a קטן has action, but his thought has no legal power.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...but they [a deaf-mute, a person who is not mentally competent, and a minor] do not have thought.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a משנה that was quoted to challenge רבי יוחנן's question about a קטן. The משנה says a קטן's actions count, but his thoughts do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן seemed unsure whether a קטן's intention counts. A משנה already says clearly that a קטן 'has no thought.' So why would רבי יוחנן ask at all? This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Thought or intention that has legal power to change a halachic status
A minor, a child who has not reached the age of מצוות
'They have action': their physical acts do have legal effect (this is the first half of the משנה's line)

phrases.english: But they do not have thought.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a משנה. 'They' means a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began just before this section, against רבי יוחנן's question about a minor's thought.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's question about whether a קטן has legal intention
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already states plainly that a קטן has no מחשבה, so there seems to be nothing left to ask.

steps.title: The question is about thought that shows in actions
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that רבי יוחנן was not asking about plain thought. He was asking about thought that can be seen from what the child does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About thought alone he has no question. Where he does have a question is when the child's thought can be recognized from his actions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers the challenge. The משנה is about pure thought, but רבי יוחנן's question is about intention that the child's actions make clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and רבי יוחנן's question are talking about two different things. A קטן's private thought clearly does not count. But when his actions openly show his intention, maybe that is enough. That is the open question.

keyTerms.meaning: Alone, by itself, with nothing added
His intention can be recognized from his actions
He has a question about it; he is unsure

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important middle category for a קטן: intention that his actions reveal. The rest of the sugya is about this category.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי חייא בר אבא is answering רבי אמי.

phrases.aramaic: מַחְשָׁבָה גְּרֵידְתָּא לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: About thought alone he has no question,
where he does have a question,
is when his thought is recognizable from his actions.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְשָׁבָה גְּרֵידְתָּא לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה by narrowing what רבי יוחנן was asking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the question is about a different situation than the one the משנה covers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was asking about plain thought, which the משנה already rules out.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was asking only about thought that the child's actions reveal, which the משנה does not address.

steps.title: Example: a child moves a burnt offering north and slaughters it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a case to show the question. A עולה stood in the south, and a child brought it to the north and slaughtered it. Did he mean it as a עולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: For example: a burnt offering was standing in the south, and he brought it to the north and slaughtered it. What is the law? Since he brought it north and slaughtered it there, does that show he intended it as a burnt offering? Or maybe he just didn't happen to find room in the south?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a concrete case that shows what 'thought recognizable from actions' means. A עולה must be slaughtered in the north, and the child took it there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the animal to the north looks like the child meant to slaughter it properly as a עולה. But there may be a simple practical reason: there was no free spot in the south. The question is whether this action is clear enough to count as intention.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering
North: the northern part of the עזרה, where a עולה must be slaughtered
He intended
It happened to be available; it came his way

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is whether a קטן may slaughter at all. His act of slaughtering does count ('he has action'). The only question is whether his move to the north shows a valid intention.

phrases.english: For example, where a burnt offering was standing in the south,
and he brought it to the north and slaughtered it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the minor. A עולה has to be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה.

phrases.english: Since he brought it to the north and slaughtered it,
he intended it [as a burnt offering],

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא מָקוֹם הוּא דְּלָא אִיתְרְמִי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is that a place did not happen to be available for him [in the south]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example that shows the narrowed question from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a קטן's action of moving a עולה to the north show enough intention to count?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן already settled this: produce on the roof
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי objects that רבי יוחנן already answered this kind of question once. He begins by quoting a משנה about produce taken to a roof and wet by dew.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this too רבי יוחנן already said one time, as we learned in a משנה: Someone who takes his produce up to the roof because of insects, and dew fell on it, the produce is not under 'when water is put.' But if he intended that, it is under 'when water is put.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי challenges the question by saying רבי יוחנן already ruled on it. Here the גמרא quotes the משנה that רבי יוחנן's earlier ruling was based on. This sets up the next move, which will show how it connects to a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce can only become able to receive טומאה (הכשר) if it gets wet in a way the owner wants, learned from the פסוק 'כי יותן.' If he brought the produce to the roof only to protect it from insects, the dew does not count. If he wanted the dew, it does count. So intention decides the law, and the next part will apply this to a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: Small insects or worms that damage produce
Dew
'When water is put' (ויקרא 11:38): the פסוק that teaches produce becomes able to receive טומאה only if wet in a way the owner wants
Making produce able to receive טומאה by getting it wet
He intended for this (for the dew to wet it)

steps.whatToRemember: The question is whether a קטן's intention counts when his actions reveal it (מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו). רבי אמי now argues that רבי יוחנן already answered this, using the משנה of produce on the roof.

phrases.english: This too רבי יוחנן said
phrases.notes: רבי אמי is speaking. He means רבי יוחנן already gave an answer to this question.

phrases.english: one time, as we learned in a משנה:
One who takes his produce up to the roof
because of the insects,
and dew fell on them,
they are not under 'when [water] is put,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:38. This means the produce does not become able to receive טומאה.

phrases.english: but if he intended for this,
they are under 'when [water] is put.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי אַמְרַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question in steps 2 and 3 by claiming רבי יוחנן already answered it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן was unsure about thought recognizable from actions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוחנן already ruled on this based on the משנה in מכשירין, it makes no sense for him to still be asking it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The משנה shows that when there is no intention, being wet does not cause הכשר, and that intention changes the result. This becomes the source for judging a קטן's intention shown through his actions.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling: a child's intention does not count
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends: if a חרש, שוטה, or קטן brought the produce up to the roof, it is not considered wet by choice, even if they wanted the dew to wet it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן took the produce up, even though they wanted it to get wet, it does not count as 'when water is placed,' because they can act, but their thought has no legal power.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי is finishing the משנה he started quoting in step 4. It says that these people's intentions do not make the produce count as wet by choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce can become טמא only if it got wet in a way its owner wanted. An adult who brings produce to the roof for the dew makes it count. A קטן does not, because his thought has no legal power. This sets up the real challenge, which comes in the next step from רבי יוחנן's comment.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When it is placed' — the פסוק that makes produce able to become טמא once it gets wet in a way the owner wanted
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor — people whose thought has no legal power
A physical action
Thought or intention that has legal power

phrases.english: If a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor took them up,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the produce from step 4, carried up to the roof.

phrases.english: even though they intended for this,
they are not under 'when it is placed,'
because they have action
but they do not have thought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quotation that רבי אמי began in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's question (step 3) about a child's visible intention
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This משנה is the base text. The challenge itself is completed by רבי יוחנן's comment on it in the next step.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן already ruled that turning the produce over counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limited the משנה: if the child turned the produce over, it does count as wet by choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The משנה only means a case where he did not turn them over. But if he turned them over, it counts as 'when water is placed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי quotes רבי יוחנן's own ruling on this משנה. That ruling shows רבי יוחנן already decided the very question he supposedly asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning the produce over shows that the child wants the dew on every side. That is thought you can see in his actions. רבי יוחנן said it counts, so why would he ask in step 3 whether a child's visible thought counts?

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this when...' — limits a ruling to a narrower case
Turned over

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִיפֵּךְ בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he did not turn them over,
but if he turned them over,
this is under 'when it is placed.'

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying a קטן's plain thought counts. Only thought that shows in what he does, like turning the produce, counts.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִיפֵּךְ בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יוחנן's comment on the משנה, which completes רבי אמי's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 3 that רבי יוחנן was unsure whether a child's visible thought counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן already ruled that a child's thought counts when it shows in his action, so he could not still be asking about it.

steps.title: The real question: Torah law or rabbinic law?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא explains that רבי יוחנן was asking whether a child's visible thought counts מדאורייתא or only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was asking: does it count by Torah law or by rabbinic law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers רבי אמי. רבי יוחנן knew that a child's visible thought counts. He was asking what level of law makes it count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling about turning produce over shows only that the thought counts in some way. It does not tell us whether the Torah itself gives it power or whether the חכמים added it. So there is still room for רבי יוחנן's question.

keyTerms.meaning: He was asking / unsure about
From the Torah itself
From the חכמים (rabbinic law)

phrases.english: This is what he was asking:
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא בר אבא answering רבי אמי. 'He' means רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Is it from the Torah or from the Rabbis?

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, everyone agrees that a קטן's visible thought counts. The only question is whether it counts מדאורייתא or מדרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether something is Torah law or rabbinic law changes how strictly we treat it. This matters most for the case in step 3, a קטן's שחיטה of a קרבן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's challenge by changing what רבי יוחנן's question was about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the question (it asks about the level of law, not whether it counts at all)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was unsure whether a child's visible thought counts at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knew it counts. He was unsure whether it counts by Torah law or only by rabbinic law.

steps.title: Another version: does a child even have legal action?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reports the exchange differently: רבי יוחנן asked whether a קטן has legally effective action at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches it this way: רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן asked: does a child have action, or does he not have action?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the whole conversation. In this version, רבי יוחנן's question is not about thought at all, only about a child's action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version assumed that a קטן has action and asked only about his thought. This version goes one level deeper and asks whether a child's action itself has legal power. That would also avoid רבי אמי's challenge, which was about thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way — introduces a different version of a discussion
Asked (raised a question he was unsure about)

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak teaches it this way:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yochanan asked:
Does a minor have action
or does he not have action?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question added on top of the first one. It is a different report of what רבי יוחנן asked in the first place.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the version given in steps 2–7 with a different version of רבי יוחנן's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a קטן's physical action has legal power at all

steps.title: Why ask about action but not thought?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי argues that רבי יוחנן's question makes no sense under רב נחמן בר יצחק's version. The same משנה rules on both thought and action, so neither should be in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Then let him also ask about thought! Why doesn't he ask about thought? Because a משנה says they have no thought? Then he shouldn't ask about action either, because the same משנה says they do have action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי challenges the idea that רבי יוחנן was asking whether a קטן's action counts at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה already says a חרש, שוטה, and קטן have action but no thought. If that settles thought, it should settle action too. So asking only about action seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Thought or intention that has legal effect
A physical action that has legal effect
Then let him ask (a challenge: why not ask this too?)
What is the difference?

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
Then let him ask about thought too!
What is different about thought
that he does not ask about it?
Because we learned: they have no thought?
Then about action too he should not ask,
because we learned: they do have action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's version of רבי יוחנן's question
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן asked whether a קטן has effective action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One משנה rules on both action and thought, so there is no room to doubt either one

steps.title: The real question: Torah law or rabbinic law?
steps.stepSummary: The question was not whether a קטן's action counts. It was whether these rules are מדאורייתא or מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was asking: is it from the Torah or from the Rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers רבי אמי by restating what רבי יוחנן was really asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells us the rules but not their source. רבי יוחנן wanted to know whether a child's action counts by Torah law and whether his lack of thought is a Torah rule. That is a real question the משנה leaves open.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah (Torah law)
From the Rabbis (rabbinic law)
This is what he was asking

phrases.english: This is what he was asking:
Is it from the Torah or from the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was asking whether a child's action counts at all
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking whether the rules are Torah law or rabbinic law

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's answer on action, thought, and visible thought
steps.stepSummary: Action counts even מדאורייתא. Thought does not count even מדרבנן. Thought that shows through action counts only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He resolves it: they have action, even by Torah law. They have no thought, even by rabbinic law. If his thought can be seen from his actions, by Torah law it doesn't count, but by rabbinic law it does.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers his own question and sets three levels for a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child's physical action is fully valid by Torah law. His inner thought means nothing at any level. In the middle is thought shown by his actions, like turning the produce over in step 6. That counts only מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And he resolved (the question)
His thought is visible from his actions

steps.whatToRemember: A קטן's action counts מדאורייתא. His thought counts not at all. His thought shown through action counts only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: And he resolves it:
They have action, even by Torah law;
they have no thought, even by rabbinic law.
His thought that can be seen from his actions:
by Torah law he does not have it,
by rabbinic law he has it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question set out in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Action counts מדאורייתא, thought counts not at all, and visible thought counts מדרבנן

steps.title: Source that acting without intent disqualifies a sacrifice
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks רב הונא for the source that a מתעסק, who slaughters without intending to slaughter, disqualifies a sacrifice.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל asked רב הונא: From where do we know that one who acts unawares with sacrifices makes them disqualified?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. שמואל asks for the source of a rule about slaughtering קדשים without intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק does the act of slaughter without meaning to slaughter at all. שמואל wants the verse that makes such a sacrifice פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who does an act without intending to do it
Sacrificial animals
Disqualified
From where (do we know)?

phrases.english: Shmuel asked Rav Huna:
From where do we know, about one who acts unawares with sacrifices,
that it is disqualified?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, also about intention in actions
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a מתעסק disqualifies קדשים

steps.title: רב הונא cites "he shall slaughter the young bull"
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers from ויקרא 1:5. The slaughter must be done knowingly, for the sake of the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And he shall slaughter the young bull," meaning the slaughter must be for the sake of a young bull.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a verse as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the verse to mean the שוחט must know he is slaughtering this animal. Someone acting unawares does not do that.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of (with intent toward)
A young bull

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And he shall slaughter the young bull,"
that the slaughter be for the sake of a young bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse requires slaughter for the sake of the bull, so knowing intent is needed

steps.title: That we know; where is it required even after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that verse only teaches what we already hold. He asks for the source that lack of intent disqualifies even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This we already have. From where do we know it is indispensable?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes back. רב הונא's verse does not prove the sacrifice is disqualified once it is already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse like this could just mean you should have intent from the start (לכתחילה). שמואל wants proof that without intent the sacrifice is פסול even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: In our hands (something we already know)
To be indispensable, so that it disqualifies even after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not rejecting the rule. He accepts that intent is needed and only wants proof that it is required even after the fact.

phrases.english: He said to him: This we already have in hand;
from where do we know it is indispensable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Says the verse in step 13 is not enough
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's source from "ושחט את בן הבקר"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse proves only the ideal practice, not disqualification after the fact
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that intent to slaughter is indispensable, so that a מתעסק disqualifies the sacrifice even after the fact

steps.title: "To your will you shall slaughter it"
steps.stepSummary: The verse in ויקרא 19:5 teaches that slaughter must be done with awareness, and that this is indispensable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: "To your will you shall slaughter it," meaning slaughter with your awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second verse that shows intent is required even after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לרצונכם" is read as "לדעתכם", meaning with your knowing intent. This makes the sacrifice valid only when slaughtered knowingly. So a מתעסק disqualifies it even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
To your will (so that it will be accepted for you)
With your awareness or intent

steps.whatToRemember: A sacrifice slaughtered without any intent to slaughter is פסול even after the fact, learned from "לרצונכם תזבחהו".

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "To your will you shall slaughter it,"
slaughter it with your awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source that intent is indispensable
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לרצונכם" means "לדעתכם", so intent is required even after the fact

steps.title: New משנה: slaughter by a gentile
steps.stepSummary: An animal slaughtered by a נכרי is a נבלה and makes a person impure by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Slaughter by a gentile makes the animal a נבלה, and it imparts impurity through carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and teaches that a נכרי's slaughter does not count as kosher slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the cut is done properly, the animal is treated like it died without שחיטה. So it has the full impurity of a נבלה, including impurity from carrying it.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (start of a new משנה)
A gentile
An animal that died without valid שחיטה
Makes a person impure by carrying it

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Slaughter by a gentile makes it an unslaughtered carcass,
and it imparts impurity through carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughter by a נכרי makes the animal a נבלה that is מטמא במשא

steps.title: The animal is a נבלה but not forbidden for benefit: who taught this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. A נכרי's slaughter makes the animal a נבלה, but not an איסור הנאה. It then asks which תנא holds this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The animal is a נבלה, yes. It is forbidden for benefit, no. Who is the תנא of our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what the משנה said and what it left out. It then asks whose opinion this is, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה called the animal a נבלה, which is forbidden to eat but may be sold or used. It did not call it forbidden for all benefit, the way an animal slaughtered for עבודה זרה would be. So the גמרא wants to know which תנא would treat a נכרי's slaughter so mildly.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without a valid שחיטה. You may not eat it, but you may benefit from it.
Something you may not use or profit from at all.
Who is the תנא? A question asking whose opinion a משנה follows.

phrases.english: GEMARA: An unslaughtered carcass, yes;
forbidden for benefit, no.
Who is the tanna who taught this?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְבֵלָה – אִין, אִיסּוּר הֲנָאָה – לָא. מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 16 and asks whose view it is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a נכרי's slaughter makes a נבלה but is not forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: Not like רבי אליעזר, who says a נכרי's thoughts are aimed at idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר holds that a נכרי's thoughts are, by default, aimed at עבודה זרה. That would make his slaughter forbidden for all benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the משנה is not like רבי אליעזר. If it were, there would be a problem, because רבי אליעזר says that a נכרי's unspoken intention is for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. The משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, a נכרי who slaughters is assumed to have עבודה זרה in mind, even if he says nothing. That would make the animal forbidden for any benefit, not merely a נבלה. Since the משנה only calls it a נבלה, it must follow a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: The default, unspoken intention of a נכרי.
Idol worship. Anything used for it is forbidden for all benefit.
Not in accordance with (a certain opinion).

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya, son of Rabbi Abba, said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer,
for if it were Rabbi Eliezer, doesn't he say:
The unspecified thought of a gentile is for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is not רבי אליעזר's view, since he holds that a נכרי's default intent is for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי אמי: a נכרי's slaughter is a נבלה, but a מין's slaughter is idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי offers a different reading of the משנה. A נכרי's slaughter only makes a נבלה, but we can infer that a מין's slaughter counts as עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: this is what the משנה teaches. The slaughter of a נכרי is a נבלה, which implies that the slaughter of a מין is for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives another way to understand the משנה. He draws the line between a regular נכרי and a מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי reads the משנה's choice of the word נכרי as meaningful. An ordinary נכרי's slaughter is only a נבלה. A מין, someone devoted to idolatry or heresy, is assumed to slaughter for עבודה זרה, so his slaughter is forbidden for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what the משנה is teaching. It introduces a reading of the משנה.
A heretic, someone devoted to idolatry or heresy.
But this one, an implied contrast.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a נכרי and a מין. In this reading, a נכרי's slaughter is a נבלה (you may still benefit from it), while a מין's slaughter is treated as עבודה זרה (no benefit at all).

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said: This is what it is teaching:
Slaughter by a gentile is an unslaughtered carcass,
but that of a heretic is for idol worship.
phrases.notes: The משנה doesn't say this out loud. רבי אמי reads it from the fact that the משנה said נכרי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 17, alongside רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה contrasts a נכרי, whose slaughter is a נבלה, with a מין, whose slaughter is for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא spells out the status of a מין's slaughter and other items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה, read this way, teaches the same thing as a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists a מין's slaughter, bread, wine, books and produce. It then begins a further opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned from the משנה what the רבנן taught: a מין's slaughter is for עבודה זרה. His bread is like the bread of a כותי, his wine is יין נסך, his books are books of sorcerers, and his produce is טבל. And some say: even…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אמי's inference matches an explicit ברייתא. It then quotes the ברייתא's list of a מין's items. The text breaks off as a new opinion begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנינא means the משנה already contains what the ברייתא says outright. This backs up רבי אמי's reading that a מין's slaughter is עבודה זרה. The ברייתא goes further and treats everything a מין makes with suspicion: his bread, wine, holy books and produce, which is treated as טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The bread of a כותי, a Samaritan.
Wine poured for idol worship. It is forbidden for benefit.
Books of sorcerers.
Produce whose תרומות and מעשרות have not been taken.

phrases.english: We learn from the mishna that which the Sages taught:
Slaughter by a heretic is for idol worship,
his bread is the bread of a Samaritan,
his wine is libation wine,
his scrolls are the scrolls of sorcerers,
his produce is untithed produce,
and some say: Even

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רבי אמי's inference to an explicit ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a מין's slaughter is considered for עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תנו רבנן) listing the status of a מין's slaughter, bread, wine, books and produce.
